title: An openEHR composition event dispatching a typed operation gives clinical data an attributed decision record
content:
openEHR models clinical information as compositions, and the demo takes a composition event as its trigger: when a clinical decision is captured, a typed operation is dispatched with it. The result pairs data that is already vendor-neutral by standard with an attributed record of the decision that produced it.

The two halves answer different questions. openEHR answers where the data can live and who can read it without a vendor's permission; the typed operation answers who decided, and in what sequence. Because Better's product is built on the standard, the demo argues from inside their own thesis rather than against it, which is a materially easier conversation than proposing a replacement.

The pairing is also the commercial argument. A vendor-neutral clinical record that cannot say who accepted a finding is incomplete for audit purposes, and an attributed decision log bound to a proprietary data model would reintroduce exactly the lock-in openEHR exists to prevent. The demo is small because it changes neither side — it only connects them.
